label: Bible Study
prompt: Let your light so _____ before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
verse: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
note: From the Sermon on the Mount — the light is for showing, the glory is for God.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you _____, even unto the end of the world. Amen.
verse: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.
note: The KJV drops the 's' — 'alway' — but the promise loses nothing: with you, all the way.

label: Sunday School
prompt: My God hath sent his _____, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.
verse: My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.
note: Daniel's morning report from the lions' den: God's angel worked the night shift.

label: Deep Water
prompt: But we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy _____; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away.
verse: But we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away.
note: Isaiah's brutal audit: even our best behavior, self-made, comes out of the wash filthy.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your _____ service.
verse: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.
note: Your 'reasonable service' — worship that makes sense. Modern versions say 'spiritual worship.'
